summary: In the subway station, Neo whip-draws his gun at lightning speed as Agent Smith opens fire. Both men blast away at impossible speed, moving through bullet-time until they are nearly on top of each other, rolling up out of a mirrored move that ends with each jamming his gun tight to the other's head. They freeze in a kind of embrace — Neo sweating and panting, Agent Smith machine-calm and smiling. Smith says Neo is empty; Neo pulls the trigger and it clicks. Neo replies that Smith is empty too. The smile falls from Smith's face; he yanks his trigger and it clicks. Smith's face warps with rage and he attacks with fists flying, Neo retreating until a knife-hand cuts his forearm and a kick slams him against a steel column. Neo ducks under a punch that crunches into the beam, steel chunks exploding. Neo leaps into the air and delivers a neck-snapping reverse round-house, sending Smith's glasses flying. Smith glares with ice-blue eyes and vows he will enjoy watching Neo die, then attacks with unrelenting fury, pounding Neo like jackhammers.

what_changes.before: Machine-calm and confident, smiling while he believes Neo has run out of bullets.
what_changes.after: His composure shatters into rage once he realises he too is empty, and he switches from gunplay to a furious physical assault.
what_changes.evidence: Agent Smith machine-calm.  Agent Smith smiles. / The smile falls.  Agent Smith yanks his TRIGGER.  CLICK. / Agent Smith's face warps with rage and he attacks, fists flying at furious speed

what_changes.before: Locked in a balanced standoff, gun to Smith's head, both equally armed and matched.
what_changes.after: Wounded and driven back — a knife-hand opens his forearm, a kick slams him against a column — losing the parity of the standoff.
what_changes.evidence: A knife-hand opens his forearm, and a kick sends him slamming back against a steel column.

what_changes.before: Even with Neo, guns jammed head to head in a mutual stalemate.
what_changes.after: Asserting dominance and relish in the kill, declaring his intention to watch Neo die before overwhelming him.
what_changes.evidence: his eyes ice blue. / I'm going to enjoy watching you die, Mr. Anderson. / Agent Smith attacks with unrelenting fury, fists pounding Neo like jackhammers.

event_hint.one_line: Neo and Agent Smith exchange gunfire to a deadlock, then to empty guns, then to a brutal hand-to-hand brawl in the subway station.

uncertain: Whether either combatant is truly gaining a lasting advantage, since the scene ends mid-fight with Smith pressing the attack.
Whether Neo's neck-snapping reverse round-house actually hurt Agent Smith or only knocked his glasses off.

minds.wants: To hold the standoff as proof that he is no longer prey — to make Smith meet him as an equal and, in doing so, confirm the belief that has just begun to form in him.
minds.feels: A raw, newly-arrived steadiness underneath the physical strain. The gunfighter's resolve from the platform (sc-180) is real but untested, so there is fear and exhaustion in the body (sweating, panting) that the will is trying to overrule.
minds.shows: Outward strain and exertion, but a flat, unflinching reply — "So are you" — delivered without flinching even with a gun to his own head. He lets Smith see effort, never doubt.
minds.basis: In sc-180 his eyes hold "something fixed and hard like a gunfighter's resolve"; sc-181 has Morpheus say "He's beginning to believe." Here he whip-draws at lightning speed, holds the gun to Smith's head, and answers Smith's "You're empty" with a level "So are you," pulling a trigger he knows clicks.

believes_about.belief: That parity is real — that if he matches Smith move for move, he can force an equal and survive the encounter on even terms.
believes_about.wrong_because: The standoff is a momentary illusion; Smith is not bound by the same limits and, once the guns are empty, simply discards the rules and overpowers him physically — the parity Neo feels is not something Smith intends to honor.

minds.wants: To reassert total control — to erase the insult of being matched by a human and to convert humiliation into the pure pleasure of domination.
minds.feels: Rage that is genuinely destabilizing. His "machine-calm" is a program's certainty of superiority, and the realization that he, too, is empty is not a setback but an outrage — something that should not be able to happen to him.
minds.shows: First a smile and a cool, almost intimate taunt ("You're empty"), then, when the click lands, the smile falls and the face "warps with rage." He narrates his own relish — "I'm going to enjoy watching you die" — turning fury into a performance of dominance.
minds.basis: He is "machine-calm" and smiling at the standoff, confident Neo is empty; the smile drops at his own CLICK, his face "warps with rage," and he escalates from gunplay to a "furious" physical assault, explicitly framing the killing as enjoyment.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is just another anomaly to be erased, and that once the tricks are spent, domination is a foregone conclusion — the smile assumes victory is already his.
believes_about.wrong_because: He reads Neo's exhaustion and the empty gun as weakness, not as the threshold of the belief Morpheus names; he does not yet understand what Neo is becoming, which is precisely why his certainty is about to be punished.

connects_back: sc-180: Neo's fixed, gunfighter's resolve on the platform is what lets him hold the gun to Smith's head without flinching.
sc-181: Morpheus's "He's beginning to believe" is the inner event this fight externalizes — Neo is testing a belief against a program that cannot be matched by old rules.
sc-179: Trinity's "Run, Neo. Run." frames Neo as prey; this scene is his first refusal of that role.
sets_up: ev-034: Smith's shift to unrelenting physical fury — and his belief that Neo is merely an anomaly to be broken — makes possible the beating in the subway and the execution-style shooting in the hotel, which in turn sets up Neo's death.

ev-034: Neo's willingness to stay in the fight on even terms, rather than flee to the exit, keeps him in the Matrix long enough to be cornered and killed — the parity he wants becomes the trap he must die in.
ev-035: The fury that drives Smith to overwhelm Neo is what strands Neo in the hotel, forcing the crew's EMP and the desperate escape that follows.
dramatic_function: To convert Neo's internal, just-born belief into a physical contest where the old rules of the Matrix break down for both combatants, and to expose Smith's fatal flaw — the certainty that a human cannot equal him — so that the story can take Neo all the way to death before the resurrection the outline promises.
